mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of 0.4 percentage points or more signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after such an unemployment spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by at least 0.5% signals a broad-based collapse in residential and non-residential demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies decline by >0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such periods of sustained payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.7% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side recovery, which lifts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4% YoY).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises >0.7% for four consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 4% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises >0.7% for four months and inflation is below 4%.
